title: Counter-Offer Conversation Guide
summary: Have this conversation at screening, not at offer stage
intro: Use at screening stage — not at offer stage. Have this conversation early.

items: Counter-offers are reactive: they rarely fix the reasons someone wanted to leave
Accepting one can change how the current employer sees them, for good
The strongest argument is always the candidate's own reasons for moving
Have this conversation at screening, not at offer stage

steps.title: Open naturally
steps.text: Before we go any further with this process, I want to have a quick conversation about something that trips a lot of people up at the end. Is that okay?

steps.title: Ask directly
steps.text: If we get to offer stage and your current employer finds out you are leaving, which they will when you hand in your notice, what do you think they will do?

steps.title: Explore the response
steps.text: And if they made you a counter-offer (matched the salary, gave you a promotion, promised things would change), what would you do?

steps.title: Address the root cause
steps.text: We spoke about why you are looking to move. A counter-offer might address the salary, but does it address the real reason you wanted to leave?

steps.title: Future pace
steps.text: If you imagine accepting the counter-offer and sitting back at your desk six months later, has anything actually changed?

steps.title: Get a commitment
steps.text: I am not trying to pressure you. But if we get to offer stage, what will you do?

title: CV Review and Submission Checklist
summary: Quality gate before sending any CV to a client
intro: Complete before sending any CV to a client. If it does not pass this gate, it does not go.

items: CV is up to date — current role, dates, and responsibilities are accurate
No unexplained employment gaps — or gaps can be explained
Formatting is clean and professional — consistent fonts, readable layout
Contact details are present and correct
No spelling errors or obvious grammatical mistakes
Dates are consistent and chronological — no overlapping roles
Most recent role is described in sufficient detail
Key skills relevant to THIS role are visible and prominent
CV length is appropriate — 2 pages for most, 3 max for very senior
The CV speaks directly to the brief — I have mentally mapped it against the must-haves
I have confirmed with the candidate that the experience described is accurate
I have flagged any gaps or concerns to the candidate before submitting
The candidate knows which role this is being submitted for and has given explicit consent
I have not submitted this candidate to the same client before (or if I have, the client is aware)

blocks.title: Key questions to ask on first contact

steps.text: I won't take much of your time. I wanted to understand a bit about where you are at with hiring before I said anything about us. What does your team look like right now?
What is the one role that, if you got it right this year, would make the biggest difference to your business?
What has been your experience with recruitment so far? Have you found it straightforward, or are there areas where you have struggled?
Are these hires you need to make in the next few weeks, or are you planning further ahead?
Is hiring something you own directly, or do you work with HR or a talent team on this?
Are you working with any agencies at the moment, or have you been going direct?
Would it be useful if I shared some market data on what I am seeing in your space: salary benchmarks, skills availability, what other companies are doing?
I would love to come back to you with something specific. Is it okay if I put together a short overview of how we work and reach out again next week?
